source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #304 (branch fix/198-aot-artifact-container at head ba0feb7de1ee4b074685e9b849f050cb0fe0be0d — the AoT artifact container for #198 (signed native-code bundle, exact-build fingerprint, fail-closed load path; commit c15d6de) on current main 04bca9a (PRs #299 and #300), plus fuzz-build fix commit ba0feb7 (enable aot-load in the fuzz crate; no embedder-linked code change); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45459026158 and 45459043471 against the branch and pull-request run 45459015271, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #304 (#198, AoT artifact container: signed native-code bundle, exact-build fingerprint, fail-closed load path). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45459064907, 45459081941 and 45459101432 on main at 04bca9a8222d11a3d8db61204440e3d74a37c949; the values reproduce the PR #302 control measurements exactly). Two effects combine. (1) Main-side baseline staleness, shared with PR #302: the checked-in baseline was measured on the PR #300 branch tree (3421c44: main 93581e8 plus PR #300) before PR #299 (precompiled-module codec, #196) merged; on the merged main, 26 of the 32 gated series differ from that baseline and most library configurations shrink (in release, stripped file -1,000 B in core to -1,896 B in wasi, stripped .text -1,056 B to -1,952 B; in release-size, stripped file -32 B to -128 B and stripped .text -16 B to -80 B where they change); the baseline configuration is unchanged in both profiles. Two of the four gate failures are this staleness alone, each +16 B: release-size core stripped .text (787,111 B to 787,127 B) and release-size wasi-threads stripped file (1,940,824 B to 1,940,840 B) — this branch is byte-identical to main on both series. (2) This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the only two configurations that link the AoT/JIT code path (core-jit and core-aot); the other six configurations are byte-identical to main on every gated series, because the new aot_artifact module is gated behind the aot-load/jit features and the unreferenced remainder is link-time eliminated in the minimal embedder. The seven differing series are: release core-aot stripped file -256 B / stripped .text -192 B, release core-jit stripped file +16 B / stripped .text -352 B, release-size core-aot stripped file +16 B (stripped .text unchanged), and release-size core-jit stripped file +384 B / stripped .text +208 B. Against the checked-in baseline the remaining two gate failures are therefore release-size core-jit stripped file +352 B (1,538,080 B to 1,538,432 B) and stripped .text +192 B (1,091,575 B to 1,091,767 B), the net of this PR's growth and the main-side shrink. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release core-nosimd stripped file series at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,792 B), followed by the release component stripped file series at +9.77% (2,433,656 B to 2,671,528 B) — unchanged from the PR #302 figures, because this PR does not grow those series. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples.
